title: Pasuwa against firing Malawi coaches ahead of Egypt tie

 Peter Kanjere · Nov 13, 2026 Kalisto Pasuwa. Photo credit: Football Association of Malawi media Faced with a daunting task against Egypt on Friday in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) group stage qualifiers, Malawi mentor Kalisto Pasuwa has cautioned against the tendency to chop and change coaches, seemingly acknowledging the precarious status of his job.
 The Zimbabwean told the Malawi FA media that changing a coach cannot transform a team, as it is the players who form the DNA; hence, the need to look at things holistically.
 His remarks come amid a run of two wins in the last six games across all competitions, the latest result being a 3-1 loss to Angola in October.
 Malawi coach comments on Egypt clash
 Sounding subdued, the tactician gave a measured assessment of the Flames' readiness for the Group B meeting against the table-topping Pharaohs, who have the odds in their favour at Cairo International Stadium.
 “I can’t comment much. The boys, according to the training sessions that we did, you could see the intensity was high. They are eager to go. In football, it is not all about coaches or what. A team can change coaches, but it is the same players. If you go further, the DNA will be the same,” Pasuwa said.
 Drawing lessons from Angola fixture
 The coach has since urged his wards to draw lessons from their last outing in Angola, where the Flames lost 3-1, largely due to late arrival to a match venue.
 “It is all about our mentality and the atmosphere. We need to quickly adjust ourselves. Last time, we arrived late and most of the things that we were doing in the first 20 minutes were slow.  We need to adjust. Now, we have done our corrections,” he added.
 Malawi will face the Pharaohs at 9 pm Southern African Time before completing the double header by welcoming the record AFCON champions at Bingu National Stadium in Lilongwe on 17 November.
 The Flames started the AFCON qualifying race with a 2-1 victory over bottom-placed South Sudan before losing to Angola, hence needing at least a point away in Egypt, where the hosts have posted seven wins against three for the Flames and the other two games ending in a draw.
 Malawi will be without defender Chembezi Denis, goalkeeper William Thole and striker Mayele Malango due to injuries, loss of form and club commitments while welcoming back John Lanjesi and Chikumbutso Salima among other players.
